resource_kind: preserved supplied-ROM bytes; no emulator capture data
algorithm: $DC07 forms home and away table bases as 11*formation (ASL; save; add formation; restore; ASL twice; add 3*formation).
Global slots 0..10 use home formation; slots 11..21 use away formation with local slot = global slot - 11.
The slot team uses $DC87 when its team base equals $05FB; otherwise it uses $DCB3. $05FB is 0 (home) or 11 (away).
$CDC9 returns x=$34+8*floor(encoded/12), y=$54+8*(encoded mod 12); nonzero $05FB mirrors each coordinate with 8-bit two's complement.
$CD7C resolves global slot through the preserved 22-word table. $DC07 stores X at record +6 and Y at record +8.

algorithm_inputs.match_index: caller-owned route context; helper supports only match 0
algorithm_inputs.possession_side_05fb: caller-owned side byte: 0 for home or 11 for away
algorithm_inputs.source_context: caller-owned decoded-game-logic context label; never a RAM/PPU capture

entries.source_role: $DC07 initializes player record positions, iterating record slots 0..21; formation bases use 11-entry rows; selects primary/secondary table and writes X/Y to offsets +6/+8.
Primary encoded position table: four formation rows of 11 player slots.

entries.source_role: Secondary encoded position table: four formation rows of 11 player slots; excludes the following adjacent byte.
$CD7C doubles a player slot and reads the corresponding little-endian record pointer at $CD89.
First 22 record pointers, mapping each global player slot to its 12-byte record in $0300..$03FC.
$CDC9 divides encoded position by $0C and returns X=$34+8*quotient, Y=$54+8*remainder.
